![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14157978/assets/71620d1e3e6691ef6c91382665fd258891984b1e32aeaec122663d65c1ca5b1b.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path along the line segment between the points $(-3,-1)$ to the point $(1,3),$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${x}_{2}=1$ and ${x}_{1}=-3.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=1-(-3)=4.
$$
